text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa is on an official visit to Macedonia. He is due to hold talks with the highest Macedonian officials and be received by Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov.
- It looks like Macedonia will have early elections following talks between Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski and Ljubco Georgievski leader of the opposition IMRO-DPMNY, commentary.

- "May 15 demonstrations will not be postponed. Our stand remains unchanged that this government should resign and that early elections are inevitable. Macedonians should express their discontent," said Ljubco Georgievski.

- Owner of bankrupt saving society TAT Sonja Nikolovska accused Macedonian National Bank governor Borko Stanoevski of being fully aware of the "problematic" situation in her bank and of giving false promises of a rehabilitation credit to TAT.
- Macedonian Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski received a group of Greek businessmen and journalists in Skopje on Thursday. He said Macedonia was interested in cooperation with Greece.
- Former Macedonian Foreign Minister Stevo Crvenkovski appointed as ambassador to London.
- Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov reiterated Macedonia's strong determination to become part of NATO in an interview to Italian La Republica. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
